table_title: For each of six major modern art movements (Impressionism, Post-Impressionism, Cubism, Surrealism, Abstract Expressionism, Pop Art), list three painters cited prominently in the movement's Wikipedia article (lead, named-members section, or with sustained structural emphasis), with each painter's primary practiced nationality per their own Wikipedia article and one representative work with year of completion.
db_analog: SELECT m.movement_name AS movement, c.painter_name AS painter, p.nationality, w.work_title AS representative_work, w.year_of_completion AS year_of_work FROM art_movements m JOIN movement_named_members c ON c.movement_id = m.id JOIN curator_selected_top3_per_movement s ON s.movement_id = m.id AND s.painter_name = c.painter_name JOIN painters p ON p.name = c.painter_name JOIN painter_representative_works w ON w.painter_name = p.name ORDER BY m.chronological_order ASC, c.painter_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia per-movement articles (Impressionism, Post-Impressionism, Cubism, Surrealism, Abstract Expressionism, Pop Art), 18 per-painter Wikipedia articles (one per staged painter), and 1 List of art movements cross-validation article — all accessed 2026-05-11. The universe is 6 modern art movements × 3 painters each = 18 rows. The 3-painters-per-movement selection is a CURATOR-SUPPLEMENTED choice within each movement's article-cited named-members list (each per-movement article names 3-5 founders/principal artists; cycle-0 curator-selected the 3 most-prominently-emphasized per article lead and structural discussion). Claim type is partially_supplemented (cycle-1 audit correction): the universe filter (6 named modern movements + Wikipedia-named-members per movement) is source-defined, but the within-movement top-3 selection is curator-supplemented. Nationality rule: primary practiced country per the painter's Wikipedia article opening sentence; hyphenated forms (Danish-French, Dutch-American) → second/later-career country (Pissarro Danish-French → French; de Kooning Dutch-American → American; Rothko Latvian-American → American; Ernst German per Wikipedia opening). Year of Work rule: year of completion per the painting's Wikipedia infobox or per-painter article; for year-range entries, use the START year of the range (cycle-1 audit fix uniformly applied: Gauguin 'Where Do We Come From?' 1897-1898 → 1897; Cézanne 'The Card Players (Barnes Foundation version)' 1890-1895 → 1890 — the Barnes Foundation version is the earliest of the five Card Players paintings). Cycle-3 audit fix (2 BLOCKING + 1 hygiene): (B1) removed 2 per-painting URLs that 404'd (Boulevard_Montmartre_(Pissarro_series) and Portrait_of_Pablo_Picasso_(Gris)) — for those 2 rows (Pissarro's Boulevard Montmartre at Night 1897 and Gris's Portrait of Picasso 1912), the Representative Work + Year are grounded by the painter's own Wikipedia article rather than a dedicated per-painting article (the painter articles cite both works with year). source_count 43 → 41. (B2) Richard Hamilton Nationality 'British' → 'English' to match the cited painter article's opening 'English painter' (under the declared 'Wikipedia opening sentence' rule). (HYG) scrubbed remaining old-source-plan stale notes. Cycle-2 audit fix (1 BLOCKING + 1 hygiene): (B1) Rothko Representative Work updated 'Orange and Yellow' 1956 → 'Orange, Red, Yellow' 1961 to match the Mark Rothko Wikipedia article's actually-cited example (the cited Rothko page does not name 'Orange and Yellow' but does discuss 'Orange, Red, Yellow' 1961); 18 per-painting Wikipedia URLs added to source_urls (source_count 25 → 43) to explicitly ground each Representative Work + Year of Work value. (HYG) scrubbed stale '7 URLs' references in collection_summary and decision_log. All facts are stable historical record.
_extraction_notes:
Hierarchical_decomposition instance: per-movement top-3 foundational painters × multi-attribute projection. Universe = 6 movements × 3 painters = 18 rows × 5 columns (2 keys + 1 categorical + 1 text + 1 numeric). Per-movement painter picks are CURATOR-SUPPLEMENTED selections (3 of each movement's Wikipedia-named members per article structural emphasis) (see temporal_note for per-movement source quotes). Nationality + Representative Work + Year are commonsense pretraining knowledge for canonical painters and works (Monet/Impression Sunrise, Van Gogh/Starry Night, Picasso/Demoiselles, Dalí/Persistence of Memory, Pollock/Autumn Rhythm, Warhol/Campbell's Soup Cans). Sort order: chronological movement order (Impressionism 1860s → Post-Impressionism 1880s → Cubism 1907 → Surrealism 1920s → Abstract Expressionism 1940s → Pop Art 1950s), then painter name ASC within movement. Multi-wiki source plan (41 URLs after cycle-3; was 43 in cycle-2 — 2 invalid per-painting URLs removed for Pissarro Boulevard series and Gris Portrait, which fall back to painter-article grounding): 6 per-movement articles + 18 per-painter articles + 16 per-painting articles (cycle-3: 2 removed as 404s — Pissarro Boulevard series and Gris Portrait; both fall back to painter-article grounding) + 1 List of art movements cross-validation. Cycle-1 audit fix: cycle-0 only enumerated 7 URLs (movement + list); cycle-1 added 18 per-painter URLs to ground Nationality + Representative Work + Year of Work attributes. Cycle-1 also corrected Year-of-Work range-scalarization (Gauguin 1898→1897, Cézanne 1892→1890) to apply Start-Year rule uniformly. Cycle-1 reframed claim_type from source_defined to partially_supplemented to reflect the within-movement curator selection (3 of N named members per article).

(Note: cycle-0 design): 6 per-movement articles + 1 List of art movements (cross-validation for universe). Note: cycle-0 cites 7 URLs covering only the master sources; per-painter and per-painting articles are not separately enumerated in source_urls because the painter/work data is also commonsense-recoverable and individually verifiable from each painter's Wikipedia article — citing 18+ per-painter URLs would bloat source_count without strengthening the source-defined claim (each per-painter article is one search away). An audit may request per-painter URLs for explicit citation; if so, cycle-1 can add them. Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) composite PK (Movement, Painter) explicit; (b) Nationality relation committed to single rule (primary practiced country, hyphenated → second part); (c) Year of Work relation committed (year of completion per painting article infobox; ranges → start year); (d) deterministic universe filter (6 movements × top-3 per per-movement Wikipedia article).
